implementation_notes: In JavaScript the poltergeist is cheap to write and cheap to remove, which is why it accumulates: `export function makeDialogHelper(v) { return { addWelcome: () => v.add(...) } }` is an object literal with a method and no state. The idiomatic replacements are a plain function (`addWelcomeDialog(view)`) and, where a method on the view is impossible, a function exported next to the module that owns the view. The JS-specific hazard is the object literal returned by a factory: it looks like a class to a reader, and its `this` binding makes it appear stateful when it is not. Object spread and `Object.assign` of a single method onto an existing object is the other shape.
idiom_name: object literal factory returning an object with one method
pitfalls: A factory returning a closure over configuration is a builder in functional dress and is fine.
Exporting an object with one method as an API shape forces every caller to destructure it, which is pure ceremony.
`Object.assign(target, { oneMethod })` monkey-patching is the same smell with the object identity preserved.
